1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4 Bc5 5..strategy: Offers the pawn back for a broad centre: the c-pawn attacks d4, which is defended only by the bishop and the knight, so Black has to decide whether to hold it. White opens lines for the pieces and is ready to play for the initiative.

Pins the knight on f3 to the queen, so that it cannot take on d4 without losing the queen, and Black can hold the pawn a little longer. It leads to sharp play with chances for both sides, with the bishop on c4 still pressing f7.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4 Bc5 5..name: Scotch Game: Scotch Gambit, Cochrane-Anderssen Variation
